notes: Both address the immediate fusion pathway claims (C14, C33, C34, C49, C51, C106). LLM finds claims UNSUPPORTED due to small sample size (7 events) and overstatement given temporal resolution. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging novelty but questioning the millisecond temporal resolution claim (actual resolution 200ms-600ms), which affects intermediate detection capability.

Both agree on stable hemifusion findings (C15, C36, C48, C107). LLM cites adequate sample size (51 hemifused cases, 2 showing delayed fusion). Peer reviewers affirm this as a central, novel conclusion about slow hemifusion-driven events with no concerns raised.

Both address complexin's effect on fusion pathways (C16, C17, C41-C43, C52-C54, C108). LLM finds SUPPORTED with adequate sample sizes (thousands of spots) and striking differences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN despite finding the concept 'appealing,' citing noisy histograms (figures 6, 8) and insufficient statistical evidence requiring more data entries.

Both agree on heterogeneous fusion pathways (C18, C19, C109). LLM notes clear documentation of immediate, delayed, and hemifusion-only pathways. Peer reviewers describe multiple fusion pathways as 'novel' and praise the 'unparalleled resolution' of the single vesicle system.

Both address cryo-EM structural characterization (C23-C32, C46). LLM finds SUPPORTED with adequate sample sizes (78, 122 interfaces; 228, 237 vesicles) and clear morphological evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, praising the cryo-EM combination as a strength but requiring histograms, classification criteria, and statistical analysis, noting 'semiquantitative' presentation without proper quantitative rigor.

Both agree that lipid mixing does not imply content mixing (C10, C11, C44, C45). LLM cites prior literature and current observations with complexin. Peer reviewers explicitly list as a central conclusion that assays measuring only membrane mixing may be misleading, with no concerns raised.

Both address experimental system capabilities (C78, C110, C112). LLM finds SUPPORTED, noting ability to discriminate fusion states on 100-ms timescale as a technical advance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, praising 'unparalleled resolution' but challenging the millisecond temporal resolution claim (actual: 200ms intervals, 600ms binning often used).

Both express uncertainty about physiological relevance of Ca2+ sensitivity (C12, C13). LLM questions whether 250-500 μM is 'reasonably close' to physiological range (starting at 10 μM), a 25-fold difference. Peer reviewers acknowledge the system is 'more physiological' but note steady-state Ca2+ for minutes differs from transient increases in transmitter release.

LLM addresses cryo-EM structural data (C23-C32, C46, C91-C92, C97) finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R5 addresses vesicle homogeneity (C70), finding it UNSUPPORTED as an 'essential assumption' requiring 'convincing evidence' not currently provided. These address different aspects of the experimental system with no direct claim overlap.
